basis: PER-JOINT MEASUREMENTS, not a formula. arm_base_joint, upper_arm_joint and fore_arm_joint were measured; the other three carry no gravity, cannot be measured by dragging, and are left at 1.0 (uncorrected) -- that is an absence of data, NOT a statement that they are correct.
measured_note: Hand-tuned with arm_drag.py until the arm floated: trim 0.2/0.3/1.1 on top of the g_scale [1.0, 1.0, 0.9683] that arm_drag resolved from source_log. arm_base and upper_arm got g_scale 1.0 because their N_tau (6.06, 3.93) fell outside G_SCALE_BAND, so their totals are the trim values verbatim.
vs_theory: The gain path gives S = N*pi, so N/S = 1/pi = 0.3183 is the scale the stray pi alone would predict. upper_arm (0.30, 6% off) and fore_arm (1.065 vs 1.0, 4% off) fit that. arm_base does NOT: it needs 0.2, a further ~1.6x below the prediction, despite being the same motor type as upper_arm. So the cause is per-JOINT, not per motor type, and these values are empirical -- do not regenerate them from a formula.
revert: Delete this file to send uncorrected torque commands.
recollect_when: Any damiao.cpp change. Re-run verify_gravity.py --fit-scale to see whether S moved, then re-tune with arm_drag.py -- the reported-torque factor N_tau in particular moves with firmware (6.06 raw vs 1.52 with TAU_MAX=112).
